message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Tests
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    name: Test suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:13
        ports: ['5432:5432']
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - name: Install Ruby
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
          ruby-version: 3.4.12
          bundler-cache: true
      - name: Install Elasticsearch
        uses: ankane/setup-elasticsearch@v1
        with:
          elasticsearch-version: 9
      - name: Verify Elasticsearch connection and create index
        env:
          ELASTICSEARCH_URL: http://localhost:9200
        run: |
          echo $ELASTICSEARCH_URL
          curl -fsSL "$ELASTICSEARCH_URL/_cat/health?h=status"
          curl -X PUT $ELASTICSEARCH_URL/joss-production
      - name: Run tests
        env:
          ELASTICSEARCH_URL: http://localhost:9200
          PGUSER: postgres
          PGPASSWORD: secret
          RAILS_ENV: test
          GH_SECRET: 12345
        run: |
          bin/rails db:create
          bin/rails db:schema:load
          bin/rails spec
",
  "rationale": "Add a custom job timeout of 10 minutes to bound runaway executions. The workflow has a representative successful-duration history (5 recent runs, 2–3 minutes each), satisfying the precondition for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT. The pattern's simulation estimate reports 12.9% free and 8.1% paid VM time reduction, and an experiment on a fork (batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) measured a 26.8% elapsed-time saving. A 10-minute limit provides ample operational headroom while protecting against stuck runs.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
